messages:
emma_sales: Heads-up: Acme POC reports 401s when hitting our inference endpoint after switching through a corporate proxy. They need a quick swarm.
acme_dev: Repro steps: requests from our dev laptop -> 200. From our CI behind the corporate proxy -> 401 Invalid API key. Same bearer token in both places.
noah_se: Curious if the proxy is injecting headers. Can you paste the raw request from CI (sanitized) incl. headers and x-rwd-request-id if present?
acme_dev: CI log: `POST /v1/inference HTTP/1.1`
`Authorization: Bearer rwd-test_prod_9a8b`
`X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45`
`X-RWD-Org-Id: org-internal`
Response body: `{"error":"Forbidden"}`
`x-rwd-request-id: rwd-req-8b77f`
kai_infra: There it is  proxy is adding X-RWD-Org-Id=org-internal. If that header doesn't match the key binding server treats it as a tenant override and will 403. Sometimes proxies strip or add headers inconsistently which can explain intermittent 401/403.
noah_se: Also check whether the proxy rewrites Authorization header (some corporate proxies mask creds). But your log shows the token present.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: looked up request rwd-req-8b77f  key fingerprint found, status: active, bound_org: org-acme, bound_project: poc-web, scopes: [inference:generate].
acme_dev: So why do we sometimes see 401 vs 403? From other runners we saw 401 Invalid API key.
kai_infra: Two reasons: 1) If proxy calls an internal cache that returns a stale/rotated key you'll see 401. 2) If header mismatch occurs it's 403. If some runners go through a path that has the header injected and others don't you'll see both codes.
noah_se: For immediate unblock: remove the injected header at the proxy or have them map it to the correct org. We can also create a short-lived key bound to the `org-internal` tenant for the PoC, but that's not ideal for long-term.
emma_sales: @acme_dev what do you prefer? Proxy change or temp key?
acme_dev: Changing proxy is slow (security team). Please create a short-lived scoped key for the CI so we can finish the demo tonight.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: created key `rwd-test_acme_proxy_13` bound_org: org-internal, bound_project: proxy-poc, scopes: [inference:generate], expires: 24h, status: active, id: rwd-test_acme_proxy_13.
acme_dev: Replaced token in CI -> Success, 200 OK, inference returns. Thanks.
noah_se: Follow-ups: 1) We'll note in the PoC runbook that proxies may inject `X-RWD-Org-Id` and to either remove it or ensure it matches key binding. 2) We'll add a quick SDK warning log when an env/org header is present and doesn't match token binding.
kai_infra: For security questionnaire: yes we support scope-limited keys for hosted PoCs, and Dedicated/Private supports CIDR/IP allowlists and HSM/KMS integrations. For hosted keys we cannot enforce per-key IP allowlist today.
emma_sales: Can we document the created temp key id and the proxy note in the CRM PoC record?
deploy_bot: crm: PoC ACME-2026-PX updated  attached key rwd-test_acme_proxy_13, note: proxy header inject mismatch, temp key expires 24h.
acme_dev: One more question: we saw a few 429s when tests ramped up. Any quick rate guidance?
noah_se: For PoC start conservative: 40	60 req/min per client, chunk embeddings, and use exponential backoff with jitter. Monitor `x-rwd-remaining` and `x-rwd-reset` headers and scale up slowly.
emma_sales: Thanks everyone. We'll keep the thread open for any follow-ups but closing the swarm for now. :white_check_mark:
